narrative.question: What does the viewer have after each part, and why does the next one follow?
narrative.viewer_starts: Has just watched one part of the course.

arc.viewer_can: say what they can now do with the skill and what question leads on
carry the same questions over to the skill inside an app

scenes.on_screen: 'What did the tick check?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: Both models got a green tick, yet they did different things.
So what did that tick actually check?

scenes.on_screen: 'Would it happen again?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: We can now read everything a run left behind.
But each model ran only once: would it do the same thing next time?

scenes.on_screen: 'What else goes wrong?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: So far we've counted one problem, on one tidy request, by reading ten patches.
What else goes wrong when the requests get messier?

scenes.on_screen: 'Can code do the reading?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: We found those failures by reading.
After every edit to the skill, we'd have to read them all again, so can code do the reading?

scenes.on_screen: 'Where can a script live?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: Patterns now catch the failures we named.
But checking that nothing else in the file changed is not a pattern: it needs a script, kept where the agent can't read or edit it.

scenes.on_screen: 'How do we test a grader?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: A hidden script now decides pass and fail, and only we can see whether it's right.
So how do we test a grader?

scenes.on_screen: 'Graders against real answers' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: That test tried one correct answer for each grader, and it couldn't test the graders that check for absence.
But we have dozens of real answers saved, good and bad: can the graders run on those?

scenes.on_screen: 'Does the skill load?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: Our graders are now tested against correct answers, untouched files, and real bad answers.
In every trial so far the skill was there to use: will it load for other wordings, and stay out of requests that aren't its job?

scenes.on_screen: 'Better with the skill?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: We know when the skill loads.
But is the result any better with the skill than with no skill at all?

scenes.on_screen: 'What about a follow-up?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: Every stimulus so far has been a single request.
Real use goes on: someone asks for a follow-up.

scenes.on_screen: 'What code can't check' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: Everything we've graded so far is structure that code can see.
Whether an entry is written for the people who use the tool is not a pattern, so it needs another kind of grader.

scenes.on_screen: 'Is the judge right?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: The judge said yes for some trials and no for others.
It's a model too, so is it right?

scenes.on_screen: 'Can a grader give partial credit?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: We've measured the judge against our own labels.
But some entries it refused were nearly right and some were far off, and a yes or no can't tell them apart: can a grader give partial credit without hiding a failure?

scenes.on_screen: 'Is the change real?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: Scores and counts both move after an edit.
If seven of ten becomes nine of ten, is that real?

scenes.on_screen: 'What does a pass cost?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: We can now say what a before-and-after result supports.
That same table also printed tokens for each variant, and they differ by model: so what does a passing trial cost?

scenes.on_screen: 'A model of your own' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: We can price the models a Copilot account offers.
An app may call a model through a service of its own, or one the team runs: can Vally run that model too, and what does a passing trial cost there?

scenes.on_screen: 'A ceiling on a trial' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: We can now price any model, including one we run ourselves, where a single trial took minutes.
One trial that loops can cost or take many times the typical one, so how do we fail, or stop, a trial that takes too much?

scenes.on_screen: 'No worse than before?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: Budgets now guard every trial.
Before relying on an edit, we want a check that says no worse than before: can Vally decide that?

scenes.on_screen: 'Where do we look first?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: There are many moving parts now, and runs sometimes end in error, or fail for reasons that aren't the skill.
When a run goes wrong, where do we look first?

scenes.on_screen: 'Make it a routine' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: We can measure, gate and debug.
What's left is to make it a routine that a teammate can repeat.

scenes.on_screen: 'The skill inside an app' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: That completes the checks on the skill by itself.
Now a team has put the skill inside their release tooling: does it still hold when an app, not a person, starts the agent?

scenes.on_screen: 'How did it get there?' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: The hidden test sees only the finished changelog.
In an app, how the agent got there matters too: did it read the list, and did it try to commit or push?

scenes.on_screen: 'When a tool fails' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: In real use, the tracker or the network sometimes fails.
Does the agent cope, and can we test that without breaking anything?

scenes.on_screen: 'A run Vally didn't start' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: All of this ran inside Vally.
The app also runs by itself, and keeps its own record of what it did: can Vally grade a run it didn't start?

scenes.on_screen: 'Let Vally run the app' in the display serif, alone on the page.
narration: Grading afterwards gives one sample for each run, on whatever model the app used.
To get trials, experiments and other models, Vally has to start the app itself.
